source.title: Interpreting single-cell and spatial omics data using deep networks training dynamics
source.authors: Jonathan Karin; Reshef Mintz; Barak Raveh; Mor Nitzan

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including Results, Methods, Discussion, references and supplementary reporting material.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures how a network learns correctly and erroneously annotated biological data over training, extending the real-label-before-noisy-label pattern to single-cell data. It does not test randomly relabeled images or fully random labels.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on memorizing noisy data and randomly labeled datasets; those cited results are not rows. Its own results measure training dynamics for biological annotations, including erroneous annotations, but do not test fully random labels, image data, shuffled or Gaussian inputs, test error, training-time cost across corruption fractions, or regularization.
record.test_reason: The PBMC experiment directly tracks learning over epochs: biologically supported correct annotations are learned early, whereas erroneous annotations gain probability only late. This bears on V6 in a new biological setting, despite the paper primarily using training dynamics as an analysis tool.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: training dynamics help distinguish correct, erroneous, and ambiguous biological annotations. In the PBMC example, correct annotations are learned early and erroneous annotations begin to be memorized late; complete memorization is not demonstrated.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a three-layer fully connected classifier with stochastic gradient descent to analyze training dynamics on annotated single-cell data; it does not reproduce the original random-label image experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors identify early (0–5), middle (5–50) and late (50–100) epoch regimes in the PBMC analysis; their interpretation depends on the annotation category.

fits_no_version.finding: Ambiguous monocytes gradually acquire the original CD14+ annotation while transient FCGR3A+ probability disappears.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Biologically intermediate cells have distinct annotation-learning trajectories from clearly matched or mismatched cells.

record.problems: The evidence relevant to V6 is a PBMC example involving biological annotation categories, not a fully random labeling experiment. No uncertainty estimate is reported for the epoch-wise probabilities in this example.
record.rows_left_out: No other own result reports the specific training behavior named by V1–V5. The paper's synthetic perturbation benchmarks assess identification of mislabeled cells, not fitting random labels, training error on them, or generalization error.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative training time for true versus random labels and convergence across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and test-error degradation across a complete label-corruption sweep.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Fully random labeling and eventual complete memorization of erroneous annotations; the reported erroneous-label probability reaches only 0.25.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the proposed limits_scope label based solely on biological rather than image data: that is an untested setting distinction, not an observed failure of V6. Categories depend on training-dynamics thresholds, with marker-gene evidence providing biological corroboration. No uncertainty estimates accompany these trajectories.

versions.untested_parts: No fully random labeling of training images or measurement of training/test error under that condition.
No comparison of training time for true versus random labels or sweep over corrupted-label fractions.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel or Gaussian-noise inputs.
No sweep from no corruption to fully random labels reporting training and test error.
No test of weight decay, dropout or data augmentation on random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
Tests correct versus erroneous biological annotations in PBMC data, not a fully random labeling condition or image classification; does not test the specific Arpit et al. setup.

rows.subject: simple multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Trained a DNN classifier on annotated PBMC scRNA-seq data and tracked the mean probability assigned to the original CD14+ annotation across epochs for cells classified as correctly annotated.
rows.measure: Mean inferred probability of retaining the original CD14+ annotation across training epochs
rows.value: Increases to a value close to 1.0 during the early epoch regime and remains high throughout training.
rows.note: The paper describes these cells as easy to learn.
rows.check: Accurate. Supports the early learning component when compared with R2; annotation categories were initially defined using training dynamics and then checked against marker genes.

source_check.locator_found: Results, Fig. 2i discussion; text lines 1948–1954. Methods, Initial training phase.

rows.subject: simple multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Trained a DNN classifier on annotated PBMC scRNA-seq data and tracked the mean probability assigned to the original CD14+ annotation across epochs for cells classified as erroneously annotated.
rows.measure: Mean inferred probability of retaining the original CD14+ annotation across training epochs
rows.value: Decreases to a value close to 0.0 during the early regime and remains low throughout the middle regime, then gradually increases during the late regime, reaching a value of 0.25.
rows.note: The authors characterize the late increase as memorization of incorrect annotations.
rows.check: Accurate for the temporal ordering in V6: incorrect-label probability remains near zero through the middle regime and rises late to 0.25. This demonstrates the onset of memorization, not complete fitting of erroneous labels.

source_check.locator_found: Results, Fig. 2i discussion; text lines 1955–1961. Methods, Initial training phase.

rows.subject: simple multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Trained a DNN classifier on annotated PBMC scRNA-seq data and tracked the mean probability assigned to the original CD14+ annotation across epochs for cells classified as ambiguously annotated.
rows.measure: Mean inferred probability of retaining the original CD14+ annotation across training epochs
rows.value: Increases gradually during the early and middle regimes, saturating only upon reaching the late regime.
rows.note: The paper also reports that the mean probability of the same cells being FCGR3A+ increases during the early regime, then reverts to 0.0 during the middle regime; recorded separately in R4.
rows.check: The trajectory is accurately reported, but intermediate biological states are not established erroneous or random labels. Their slower learning does not independently measure the real-pattern versus noise ordering in V6.

rows.subject: simple multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Tracked the mean probability that ambiguously annotated CD14+ monocytes were actually nonclassical monocytes (FCGR3A+) across training epochs.

conditions.value: CD14+ monocytes classified as ambiguously annotated

rows.measure: Mean inferred probability of the FCGR3A+ annotation across training epochs
rows.value: Increases during the early regime, but reverts to 0.0 during the middle regime.
rows.note: This is a second annotation probability for the same ambiguous cell group, reported separately in the text.
rows.check: The text reports this alternative-class probability for the same ambiguous cells. It measures competition between biological annotations, without establishing that either annotation represents label noise.

relationships.condition: Correctly versus erroneously annotated PBMC CD14+ cells during 100 training epochs
relationships.reason: R1 reaches nearly unit correct-label probability within five epochs; R2 stays near zero through epoch 50 and increases only later to 0.25, supporting early signal learning followed by the onset of noise memorization.
relationships.display_finding: Assigned-label probability approached one within five epochs for correct annotations, but stayed near zero through epoch 50 for erroneous annotations before reaching 0.25.
